sentences.text: The case was registered by the Mannarkkad police as per the direction of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Mannarkkad under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C in a complaint preferred by the de facto complainant against her husband, mother-in-law and sister-in-law who were arraigned as Accused Nos.1 to 3.

On the basis of the final report filed by the S.I of Police, Mannarkkad, the learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence under Section 498A read with Section 34 I.P.C and issued summons to Accused Nos.1 to 3.
In the trial that followed, six witnesses were examined from the part of the prosecution as PW1 to PW6 and two documents were marked as Exts.P1 and P2.
Though the accused were given opportunity for defence evidence, after questioning them under Section 313 Cr.P.C, they did not prefer to adduce any evidence.

After evaluating the evidence adduced, and hearing both sides, the learned Magistrate found all the accused not guilty of the offence under Section 498A I.P.C read with Section 34 I.P.C, and acquitted them under Section 248(1) Cr.P.C.
Aggrieved by the above acquittal, the de facto complainant has come up with the present revision petition.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner, the learned counsel for respondents 1 to 3 and the learned Public Prosecutor who represented the 4th respondent.
4.

The learned counsel for the revision petitioner would contend that the trial court went wrong in discarding the evidence adduced by the revision petitioner as PW1 with regard to the cruelty meted out to her by the accused.
It is also pointed out that the oral evidence adduced by PW1 in the above regard was corroborated by the evidence of PW2, the father of PW1.

5. A reading of the impugned judgment of the trial court would reveal that sufficient reasons are stated for discarding the evidence adduced by PW1 with regard to the charge levelled against the accused.

The learned Magistrate has observed in the impugned judgment, on the basis of the evidence of PW2, that a complaint which PW1 preferred before the Police about 10-20 days prior to the filing of Ext.P1 complaint before the Court, was compromised by virtue of a written agreement between PW1 and the accused, and that the failure of the first accused to abide by the terms of the above agreement had prompted PW1 to file this complaint.

The trial court has also taken note of the fact that there is no medical evidence pointing to the injuries sustained by PW1 as a result of the alleged physical assault perpetrated by the first accused.
It is after appreciating all the above aspects that the court below arrived at a conclusion that there is no believable evidence to show that the accused committed the offence alleged against them.
6. There is absolutely nothing on record to show that the finding of the court below in the above regard was grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable.
It is also not possible to hold that the court below wholly ignored material facts and exercised the judicial discretion arbitrarily or capriciously.
In the above circumstances, it is not possible for this Court to interfere with the findings of the court below.

Therefore, I am of the view that the impugned judgment of the court below, acquitting the accused in respect of the charge under Section 498A read with Section 34 I.P.C, is not liable to be interfered with in this revision.
In the result, the revision fails, and it is accordingly dismissed.
